## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `BULLET_HINT` matches the validator. The new `CRITERION_HINT` does not: it tells users to leave out "shall", but the `require_shall` option, which the PR says it keeps, rejects any criterion without " shall ". This contradiction should be resolved before merge.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — `CRITERION_HINT` now says "Write criteria as direct action bullets without the word shall." When `require_shall=True` (still a supported option; see `config.example.yml:1`), `accepts_criterion` at `app/criteria.py:7-8` returns `" shall " in text`. So a bullet written exactly as the hint says, like `- Save the result`, is rejected, and `tests/test_criteria.py:20-21` asserts that rejection. Could you make the hint depend on the option (for example, a separate hint when `require_shall` is set), or word it so it doesn't forbid "shall"? — Anyone running with `require_shall: true` who follows the hint will have every criterion rejected, and the hint gives them no way to see why.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The new `BULLET_HINT` ("Start each criterion with a dash and a space (`- `).") matches the `text.startswith("- ")` check at `app/criteria.py:5` exactly.
- The validator logic and its tests are unchanged. The existing tests still cover both `require_shall` values for bulleted and non-bulleted input.
